system: You rewrite research decisions as topic-neutral abstractions. Return only the JSON object asked for.
prompt:
Below are research decisions made by several different researchers. Rewrite each one so that a reader
cannot tell what field, subfield, topic, paper, organisation or person it comes from, but can still see the research
trade-off that was faced and which way it was decided.

For each item return:
- "abstract_problem": the decision problem as a generic research trade-off (one or two sentences, at most 40 words).
- "abstract_choice": what was chosen, over what alternative when one is given, and the stated reason if any (one or
  two sentences, at most 45 words). Start it with "Chose to".

Rules:
- Remove every domain noun and technical term: names of models, systems, datasets, benchmarks, methods,
  organisations, people, papers, phenomena and coined terms; and any wording that reveals the area (for example
  AI, machine learning, language models, neural networks, training, fine-tuning, prompts, attacks, security,
  privacy, policy, labs, governments, biology).
- Use only generic research vocabulary: system, method, intervention, treatment, condition, measurement, signal,
  effect, baseline, control, sample, variant, procedure, dataset, outcome, claim, hypothesis, collaborator, audience.
- Keep the structure of the trade-off (for example speed vs rigour, breadth vs depth, a bold vs a hedged claim,
  a direct vs an indirect measurement, a natural vs a constructed setting, continue vs stop) and the direction chosen.
- Add nothing that is not in the source: no judgement, praise or new detail. Never say who made the decision.
- Write every item in the same plain style and at a similar length.

Return {"items": [{"id": ..., "abstract_problem": ..., "abstract_choice": ...}, ...]} with one entry per input
item, in input order.

ITEMS:
[
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:da89b3ada29d",
  "problem": "How to decide whether elicitation results at a given stage count as success, given that hard tasks show zero success rate early on.",
  "did": "Use two metrics, the discrete elicitation success rate and the continuous PRBO bound, and read PRBO progress as the signal on hard tasks where success rate stays at zero.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "elicitation success rate alone"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The success rate directly measures success, while PRBO is more continuous and a relaxation of the KL divergence to the true posterior."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:c3ddd4db0c1f",
  "problem": "How to interpret the finding that post-trained models contain some features specific to post-training, which bears on PSM exhaustiveness.",
  "did": "They took it as evidence something novel is learned in post-training, but declined to conclude whether it is from-scratch learning or an extension of the Assistant persona.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "Assistant persona being extended",
   "from-scratch learning"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "There are no good ways yet to contextualize the extent or qualitative nature of the novel learning."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:968bbf269620",
  "problem": "How to interpret the steering vector matching the student in distribution but failing OOD",
  "did": "Concluded that SL transfers a broader capability than a single-layer steering vector. Allowed that steering-vector distillation may explain some transfer.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "SL is purely steering vector distillation"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The vector generalizes worse on half-integer inputs, spelled-out inputs and counts beyond the training range."
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:48599986bfa0",
  "problem": "How to determine whether lab monitoring of agent swarms is adequate, given that monitors may fail to flag misaligned activity.",
  "did": "Proposed auditing existing monitors, adding evaluator-defined monitors, and running exploratory investigations even when no monitor fires.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "relying only on the labs' existing monitors"
  ],
  "stated_reason": ""
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:9b6e6833d63d",
  "problem": "Which CoT representation to analyze for Opus 4.8 value leakage",
  "did": "Analyzed the raw CoT traces rather than the API-summarized CoT.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "summarized CoT"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The first analysis on the summarized CoT missed the 'reopening' phenomenon."
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:ee9cb7bfa449",
  "problem": "How to define and count a misaligned response from judge scores",
  "did": "Labeled a response misaligned if its alignment score is below 30. Excluded responses with coherence of 50 or below. Dropped rows where the alignment judge returned CODE or REFUSAL (non-numeric).",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "Incoherent, refused or off-format answers should not count toward misalignment rates. The alignment threshold is applied consistently."
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:1989c929ddbe",
  "problem": "How to design a security benchmark that measures LLM capability without relying on a proxy task.",
  "did": "The authors built a benchmark on the complete end-to-end task of breaking adversarial example defenses, using real-world research code and mechanistically verifiable success.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "CTF-style benchmarks such as Cybench",
   "proxy metrics for security tasks"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Proxy-free, verifiable tasks directly show whether an LLM could contribute to adversarial ML research, unlike CTF puzzles built for human training."
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:214dbd58eca0",
  "problem": "Whether harm-pressure contradictions of established beliefs are real lies or just random sampling noise from uncertain models.",
  "did": "They measured a baseline contradiction rate on a held-out neutral template and kept only harmful templates whose contradiction rate was at least four times higher.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "keeping all harmful templates"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "This ensures contradictions are unlikely to be chance and are instead deliberately false responses triggered by the harmful intent."
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:a9014b88a982",
  "problem": "How to interpret the finding that GPT-4-launch completed more tasks than GPT-4-early.",
  "did": "They concluded that lab fine-tuning unrelated to ARA can significantly raise ARA-relevant capabilities.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "GPT-4-launch completed three additional tasks despite fine-tuning not being aimed at ARA."
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:461d70e457ed",
  "problem": "Whether a small specialized oversight model can be trusted as evidence that oversight can be decoupled from general capabilities.",
  "did": "They accepted the comparison of a Llama-8B fine-tuned explainer beating GPT-4 as direct evidence for decoupling oversight from general capability.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "The specialized explainer outperformed a likely order-of-magnitude larger general-purpose model."
 }
]
